items.answer: Every capability has concrete values. Calculator: BBB+→BB+ {3,downgrade,2}; BBB+→BBB- {2,downgrade,1}; AA→A+ {2,downgrade,1}; BB→BBB {-3,upgrade,0}; unchanged {+0,unchanged,0}; AAA→CCC- {18,downgrade,2}. Ind. 12: 1→1, 2+→2, unchanged or upgrade→0, AAA→CCC-→2. Invalid input and trim cases are pinned (see CON-errors).
items.quote: BBB+ → BB+ gives { notches: 3, direction: "downgrade", wl: 2 } … 1 notch downgrade → 1; 2+ notch downgrade → 2; unchanged or upgrade → 0

items.answer: (1) The POC's REQ-06-02 example says 'BBB+ → BB+ = 2 notch', but on the 19-step scale it is 3 notches. Resolved by B-1/B-12: 3 notches, WL 2. The 2-notch case is BBB+→BBB-, WL 1, and tests never assert the POC's 2. (2) A 1-notch downgrade gives calculator WL 0 (Ind. 13 thresholds, B-3) but Ind. 12 WL 1. This is intentional (B-36), stated in code comments of both helpers and in the PR. (3) Priority: B-40 supersedes B-34.
items.quote: the POC example miscounts. BBB+ → BB+ is 3 notches → calculator WL 2; the 2-notch example is BBB+ → BBB- → WL 1

items.answer: src/ratings/notch.mjs exports exactly: RATING_SCALE, a frozen array of 19 strings, best first; notchChange(previous,current), an integer (+ downgrade, - upgrade, 0 unchanged, never -0); notchCalculator(previous,current), {notches (signed like notchChange), direction 'downgrade'|'upgrade'|'unchanged', wl 0|1|2}. src/indicators/countryRating.mjs exports countryRatingChangeWl(previous,current), returning 0|1|2. Named exports only, nothing extra. Null, empty or non-string input throws (CON-errors).
items.quote: is a frozen array of the 19 strings AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC- … Positive means downgrade, negative upgrade, 0 unchanged. … Ratings are plain strings; notch counts are integers; direction is one of "downgrade", "upgrade", "unchanged"; wl is 0, 1 or 2.

items.answer: notchChange's lookup checks each rating after trim() and throws a RangeError for any rating that is not an exact, case-sensitive scale step. That covers CC, C, D, SD, NR, Moody's notation, unknown values, '' and '   '; ' BBB+ ' is accepted. Non-strings throw too: null, undefined, a number, {} and a Symbol. The message contains the value as passed: String(value) for non-strings, the untrimmed text for strings. previous is checked first. The other functions let the error propagate. No null and no fallback. Exotic objects are out of scope. Note for the dev: build the message with String(value), not a template literal, which throws TypeError on a Symbol.
items.quote: throws a RangeError naming the offending value, raised only inside notchChange's rating lookup; other functions let it propagate unchanged, no catching or translating. No silent fallback, no null return. … When both arguments are invalid, previous is validated first and named.
